_note: Division keywords are Python regular expressions. A record joins a division when its title or summary matches one of the division's keywords, or when the source query that produced it belongs to the division. Matching is mechanical and reproducible; it is a filing system, not a finding.

divisions.title: Corporate power and antitrust
divisions.scope: Mergers, acquisitions, minority stakes and interlocks; monopolization and exclusionary conduct; merger review outcomes; consent decrees and their enforcement.
questions: Which acquisitions or minority investments by watched entities avoided or survived merger review, and on what stated grounds?
Where has a regulator alleged exclusionary conduct, and how did the matter end (judgment, settlement, closure, still pending)?
Which investor-partner-customer loops (one firm funding another that then buys from it) appear in filings?

divisions.title: AI infrastructure accountability
divisions.scope: Model developers, chipmakers, compute providers and their financing: OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, xAI, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, CoreWeave, Oracle and others treated identically. Compute commitments, circular financing, government contracts, export controls, disclosures of risk.
questions: What do the AI developers' own filings say about who owns them, who supplies their compute, and on what terms?
Which chip, cloud and model companies are each other's investors, suppliers and customers at the same time?
What public money (contracts, grants, tax incentives) flows to AI developers and compute providers?

divisions.title: Financial conglomerates
divisions.scope: Large banks, asset managers, private equity and payment networks: common ownership, systemic size, enforcement history, consumer harm documented in complaint data, and their financing of the other divisions' subjects.
questions: Which asset managers hold large stakes across competing firms in the same market?
What enforcement actions have bank regulators taken against watched institutions, and were penalties paid?
Who financed the AI and data-centre build-out (debt, private credit, SPVs), and what do the filings say about the terms?

divisions.title: Cloud and data gatekeepers
divisions.scope: Hyperscale cloud, search, app stores, data brokers and credit bureaus: control points over data, distribution and switching; privacy enforcement; interoperability and egress.
questions: Where do cloud providers hold equity in the AI developers that are their largest customers?
What enforcement or market investigations target search, app-store, cloud or data-broker conduct?
Which data gatekeepers generate the most documented consumer complaints, and how do they respond?

divisions.title: Essential services concentration
divisions.scope: Electricity, grid and generation (including data-centre power deals), telecom and broadband, health insurance and pharmacy benefit management: consolidation and its effect on prices and access.
questions: Which utility mergers or long-term power deals for data centres were reviewed, and what conditions were imposed?
Who bears the grid and generation costs created by data-centre demand?
Where do health insurers, PBMs or telecom carriers hold concentrated regional positions under regulatory review?

divisions.title: Regulatory capture and consumer protection
divisions.scope: Lobbying spend and registrations, rulemaking and its withdrawal, enforcement closures, revolving-door appointments, deceptive or unfair practices, refunds and penalties actually paid.
questions: How much do watched entities report spending on federal lobbying, through which firms, on which issues?
Which rules or enforcement matters were withdrawn, narrowed or closed, and what reason was given on the record?
Where regulators announced consumer redress, is there a record that it was paid?
